description: USFS Climate Gallery - Forest Disturbances and Drought is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFS Office of Sustainability and Climate; USFS Geospatial Technology and Applications Center. Disturbances are events that may result in short- or long-term changes in an ecosystem. Droughts and extreme weather may directly or indirectly cause disturbances to forests and rangelands in the United States. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Landslides, Vector-Borne Disease, Wildfire, High Winds, Drought, Water Quality, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems. Assets: Natural Areas and Wildlife, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
